_notes.usage: Copy this file to config.json and fill in real values. config.json is gitignored-by-convention and should never be committed (it holds credentials).
_notes.snapshot: Every camera is pulled via a single HTTP GET to its snapshot endpoint (e.g. a Bosch dome's /snap.jpg), authenticated with HTTP Digest, using one common username/password for ALL cameras -- there's no per-camera override and no RTSP/Genetec path anymore (removed in favor of this). During a collection window the service polls this endpoint repeatedly (as fast as the HTTP round trip allows, or paced by poll_interval_ms) instead of decoding a continuous video stream. Chosen because trigger events here are trucks crawling in slowly, not fast drive-bys, so RTSP's much higher frame rate wasn't needed to catch a good shot.
_notes.snapshot.url_template: Default matches a Bosch FLEXIDOME 3000i/5000i's snapshot path: http://ip:80/snap.jpg. Confirm on your specific unit's web UI under RTSP/streaming (or HTTP) settings if snapshots fail or come back low-res.
_notes.alpr.expected_frame_width/height: Set to your camera's real sensor resolution (e.g. a 5MP camera is commonly 2592x1944) to catch the snapshot endpoint unexpectedly serving a lower-res image than the camera's actual sensor. Leave both null to disable the check.
_notes.logging.level: Text log verbosity: DEBUG / INFO / WARNING / ERROR. Independent of alpr.diagnostics_mode below, but diagnostics_mode='troubleshooting' forces this to DEBUG regardless of what's set here.
_notes.alpr.diagnostics_mode: 'basic' (default): saves the first fetched frame + its ROI crop, the selected plate crops, and the OCR-prep images -- fine for normal operation. 'troubleshooting': all of that PLUS every fetched frame (full image and ROI), the ROI annotated with every box the model returned (green=kept, red=rejected-by-size/position, orange=rejected-as-duplicate, with the rejection reason labeled), and every raw candidate crop saved the instant it's found rather than just the final best_samples -- and forces logging to DEBUG. Use this to see WHY, e.g., raw_cands stays at 0 (wrong ROI vs. camera framing? model detecting nothing at all vs. detecting boxes but all getting filtered out?). Generates a lot more files per event -- meant to be turned on temporarily while diagnosing, then switched back to 'basic'.
_notes.alpr.upper_half_fraction: A detected box is rejected as 'upper_half' if its vertical center sits above this fraction of the ROI's height (0.45 = reject anything in the top 45%). Meant to filter false positives from cab signage/mounting hardware above the real plate -- but if your camera's mounting angle puts the real plate legitimately high in the ROI, this will silently discard correct detections (confirmed via diagnostics_mode='troubleshooting': the model boxed the plate correctly but it was labeled upper_half). Lower it (e.g. 0.15) or set to 0 to disable the check entirely if that happens.
_notes.event_filter: Trigger events carry a VCA classification per detected object, e.g. Data.Object.Object.Appearance.Class.Type = {"#text": "Vehicle", "@Likelihood": 0.91}. Only events with a detection matching one of class_types (case-insensitive) at or above min_likelihood are queued for ALPR -- everything else (Person/Bicycle detections, low-confidence hits, events with no classified object) is discarded before a single snapshot is fetched. Tune min_likelihood against the values your camera actually reports (0.91 in the sample payload this was built from).
_notes.event_filter.class_types (disabling): Set class_types to an empty array, [], to disable this filter entirely and queue EVERY line-crossing event regardless of classification -- min_likelihood is then ignored too. Do not just delete min_likelihood or set it to 0/null while leaving class_types non-empty -- the event still has to match one of class_types first, so that alone would not stop filtering.
_notes.alpr.publish_no_valid_plate: false (default): when a collection finds no valid plate, the result is still written to the audit folder (result.json/event.json) but NOT published to MQTT -- cuts down noise on the result topic to just actual reads. Camera/system errors (CAMERA_UNREACHABLE, CAMERA_CONFIG_ERROR, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, ERROR) are unaffected and always publish. Set true to publish every result, including plain misses.
_notes.mqtt.subscribe_topic (filtering): Which rule/event types reach this service at all is decided HERE, by MQTT's own wildcards, not by any code-side filtering -- the broker only ever delivers topics matching this filter. A real observed topic looks like 'Camera_Events/AR-M4/onvif-ej/RuleEngine/LineDetector/Crossed/&1/Crossing line 1' (bay='AR-M4' is segment 1). A sibling topic for a different rule ('.../RuleEngine/FieldDetector/Crossed/&1/Entering field 2') has the exact same shape except the detector type -- '+' matches exactly one topic segment, '#' matches all remaining segments (only valid at the end). So 'Camera_Events/+/+/RuleEngine/LineDetector/Crossed/#' matches every bay's LineDetector/Crossed events (and their varying '&1/<free text>' suffix) while never even delivering FieldDetector (or any other rule type) to this service. Widen it (e.g. drop the /LineDetector/Crossed segments back to '#') only if you want every rule type delivered here -- in that case matches_class_filter (event_filter below) becomes the only thing protecting against non-vehicle events.
_notes.mqtt.bay_segment_index: 0-based position of the bay name within subscribe_topic, e.g. 1 for 'Camera_Events/<bay>/...'. Adjust if your topic layout puts it somewhere else.
